Arab Kings.
There was another emir there named Arslan,
and the mother of the boy,
and he killed Bazmish,
and took her as his wife.
And while he was inflicting many evils upon the people of Melitene in collecting gold,
that mother of the boy made an agreement with the boy, her son,
and they seized Arslan and imprisoned him,
and it was thought that he was killed.
And after a year they brought him out,
and sent him to Sultan Ghiyath al-Din in Khorasan.
And that sultan sent Malikshah, the son of Qilij Arslan, to Melitene,
and he was proclaimed king.
And he released Toghril Arslan, his younger brother,
and imprisoned his other two brothers, Mas'ud and 'Arab.
And when that Malikshah remained for years in Melitene,
and was hard pressed
by the son of Danishmend,
he went to Alexios {OCR?}, emperor of the Greeks, so that he might help him.
And he was received joyfully,
and much gold was given to him.
And when he departed,
the son of Danishmend set ambushes for him, seized him,
and blinded his eyes.
Then the emirs who were in Melitene brought Mas'ud out of prison,
and proclaimed him sultan.
And that Mas'ud left 'Arab and Toghril Arslan, his brothers, in Melitene,
while he himself went to Iconium,
and made it his royal residence.
And in the year 1421
of the Greeks
(1110 of our Lord), the Franks took the city of Tripoli from the Arabs,
after seven years of warring against it.
And after a year Tancred, king of Antioch, went out with a large army of Franks,
and they captured many fortresses,
and took them from the Arabs,
and killed everyone who was found in them.
And they came to Manbij,
and did not find anyone in it.
And likewise in Balash they found no one;
and they cast fire into it and burned it down.
And they returned to Tripoli so that their horses could graze on grass in the spring and then return.
And when the Arabs of Syria were placed in great fear of them,
they had no recourse except to appease the Franks with gold.
Therefore Ridwan, the lord of Aleppo, sent to Tancred, the Frankish king, thirty-two thousand dinars,
and twenty Arabian horses,
and forty exquisite garments.
